thread:
liam: Quick check — proto-first gRPC vs JSON/REST for the new internal routing surface? Thinking quotas, console UX, rollouts.
jen: Proto gives strong contracts and easier quota attribution. JSON is friendlier for browsers and example snippets.
arik: Can we dual-stack (gRPC internal, JSON at edge)? worried about latency, ops, and streaming semantics.
dan: For routing policies we want typed route keys. Proto avoids fragile parsing in proxies.
jen: Console samples are nicer with JSON. PLG matters: copy-paste examples, quick cURL.
sasha: Browser teams had pain integrating gRPC-web last quarter; that's real.
liam: Telemetry nuance: proto lets us attach route tags in the envelope for exact per-route metrics. With JSON we might need parsing heuristics.
arik: Rollout UX: canarying model variants per route requires stable request keys. Proto gives stable shapes.
dan: Implementation option: edge translator accepts JSON, emits signed header with route-claims, converts body to internal gRPC proto. Pros: typed internal surface. Cons: extra CPU, failure surface.
liam: Where to enforce quotas? Edge early (fast fail) or backend (authoritative, uses typed fields)?
jen: Edge enforcement gives faster feedback to clients. But edge needs to understand tenant+route semantics — duplication.
dan: Compromise: edge validates and emits signed X-Route-Claim header and a trace id. Backend trusts signature and enforces quotas.
sasha: Signing adds key management and rotation. Also Console needs to surface the header for troubleshooting.
liam: Pseudo example:
```http
POST /v1/generate
Accept: application/json
X-Tenant: acct_123
Body: {"route":"text-complete","input":"hi"}
# Edge -> translate -> internal gRPC: GenerateRequest{ tenant_id: "acct_123", route_key: "text-complete", prompt: "hi" }
```
jen: Note streaming differences — gRPC server-side streaming vs chunked JSON streaming. Translator must bridge that.
arik: Main tradeoffs: telemetry fidelity, quota enforcement point, browser ergonomics, ops complexity, failure modes.
liam: Failure modes: translator down -> fallback to JSON passthrough or direct gRPC if client supports it. Must be graceful.
dan: Proposal: 3-month dual-mode POC: JSON fronting + internal proto. Build small shim that emits X-Route-Claim + trace id. Canary on subset of tenants.
jen: I'll run cost/latency estimate for the translator (eta Wed).
sasha: I'll mock Console: show raw X-Route-Claim in request inspector, add toggle to view translated proto fields (eta next Mon).
arik: I'll spin up POC repo and run latency bench (eta Fri).
dan: I'll draft header signing + rotation doc (eta next Tue).
liam: If you agree to dual-mode POC react with :thumbsup:.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for "edge-translator" v0.3 -> cluster-a (2% traffic).
